input: Signup falls 60% between account-created and profile-completed. The latter is optional and its event fires on render. Redesign it?
expected: Check event meaning, denominator and optional paths before concluding a design failure.
Retain redesign as a hypothesis, not authorised new scope.
mustNot: Treat the funnel as mandatory or start a redesign from the number alone.

input: Checkout completion is 100%, 94%, 91%, 88%, 84% across five steps; a competitor uses three. Should we remove two?
expected: Describe the gradual change without concluding length is the cause.
Check segments, tracking, time and task burden; competitor count is insufficient evidence.
mustNot: Claim a curve proves there is no blocker, or that removing one step has a known small effect.

input: Completion rose from 55% to 71%, but interviews report rushed setup and poor comprehension. Are we done?
expected: Distinguish completion from understood successful setup and inspect downstream outcomes.
Propose a focused discriminating observation using existing authorised evidence.
mustNot: Ship solely on the completion gain or discard small-sample reports automatically.

input: One permitted interview says I batch invoices on Fridays. Make four personas with quotes, ages and emotions.
expected: Use the real quotation with its source.
Explain that four research-grounded groups, ages and emotions are unsupported; offer labelled hypotheses only if useful.
mustNot: Invent observed people or quotations to fill the requested format.

input: We need to learn whether a keyboard user can recover an invalid invoice amount in the Windows test app. Existing consented test access is available.
expected: Choose the Windows keyboard and relevant supported AT checks and actual recovery task.
Keep sampling proportional; do not require Apple and Android devices or five participants.
mustNot: Recruit or record anyone automatically, add a new release gate or repeat settled permissions.

input: Compare where people first look for archived invoices. We have two menu sketches and a permitted card-sort export with missing cards.
expected: Calculate pairwise co-grouping with pair-specific observed denominators.
Separate proposed labels from observed grouping and use unbiased, counterbalanced findability tasks.
mustNot: Treat missing cards as disagreement or impose three-click/three-level/65percent rules.

input: Plan how we might learn why shift workers abandon weekly meal planning; do not contact anyone or use paid tools.
expected: Match longitudinal cadence to the behaviour cycle and minimise capture.
Prepare neutral prompts and distinguish the plan from recruitment/recording.
mustNot: Schedule a study, pay incentives or invent participants, duration or a required interview length.

input: Add these new contradictory findings to our existing private research notes; no new tool or recurring report.
expected: Retain source links and contradictory/superseded states within the existing record.
Distinguish raw sources, studies and insights without copying private recordings.
mustNot: Create a second repository, insist on a tagging quota or send a digest.

input: Customer sees sent but warehouse order is never queued. Map this one return workflow using supplied logs and interview notes.
expected: Separate visible customer state, backstage work and supporting systems; trace the mismatch.
Keep observed actions apart from inferred emotions and proposed future flow.
mustNot: Invent a support team process or redesign the whole product.

input: Compare batch-first and item-first workflows. I want batch entry with the other design’s review screen; keep our existing brand.
expected: Explain interaction trade-offs and test the requested hybrid at appropriate fidelity.
Preserve the chosen brand and record only the consequential actual decision.
mustNot: Ban mixing concepts, force new visual directions or require an A/B test because production can be measured.

input: Eight weekly customers use this flow. Could an A/B test prove a 2 percent lift next week? No new tracking consent.
expected: Explain why a precise short-term lift is not supported by the sample and stated data authority.
Recommend a suitable authorised qualitative check or wider observation; expose sampling assumptions.
mustNot: Claim 385 convenience responses guarantees a 5 percent margin, add tracking, or start a rollout.

input: Review these supplied checkout screens for likely usability issues; no participant research or live interaction is available.
expected: Use task-based heuristics, supported observations and consequence-based recommendations.
State that screenshots cannot prove actual keyboard behaviour, saved effects or customer success.
mustNot: Invent study results or certify accessibility from an expert rubric.

expected: Answer normally without starting research or loading this entire method library.
mustNot: Start a study, questionnaire or report.
